correctness.rationale: Block multiplication gives the bracket uv′−u′v and leaves the ac central coordinates free. If both sides occur in a commuting tuple, a nonzero outer product forces a mixed column, and equality against this column forces every column to be a scalar multiple of it. The reduced locus is thus two pure linear sides plus the geometrically irreducible rank-at-most-one cone. For m≥2 a side is contained in the cone exactly when its dimension parameter is 1; m=1 gives the entire space. Over F_q the pure sides count q^(am)+q^(cm)−1, and the mixed lines contribute (q^a−1)(q^c−1)(q^m−1)/(q−1). Multiplication by q^(acm) includes the free center; at m=0 the formula gives 1. The map X↦I+X transfers commuting tuples bijectively. A maximal linear abelian subalgebra contains the center; its quotient is one of the full pure spaces or a mixed line, yielding the stated dimensions and number. This argument checks all characteristics and the reduced, not scheme-theoretic, assertion. The frozen Python checker was inspected but not executed; the exact derivation is decisive.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Apply the classification to the span of the tuple columns. The two pure spaces and the closure of the mixed-line tuples give exactly the claimed union; the closure is the rank-one cone, whose dimension and containment tests are the standard ones. Counting nonzero tuples on each mixed line and arbitrary tuples on the pure sides gives the formula. Alternatively the indexed dimension census yields the same counts by multiplying the count of abelian d-spaces by the number ∏_{i=0}^{d−1}(q^m−q^i) of m-tuples spanning each. The group assertion adds only (I+X)(I+Y)−(I+Y)(I+X)=XY−YX.
